svg.title: Electronics schematic
svg.text: Poké Ball in the tall grass: every pad of every board, the empty ones included. Pin map and values as in docs/electronics.md.
Adafruit 3006 or a copy of it
On the board: replace R_PROG, 1.2 kΩ,
by 2.0 to 2.4 kΩ (charges with about 0.5 A).
USB 5 V, live only while the XIAO's own USB-C is plugged in
strapping pin of the chip, leave open
debug TX; the chip prints its boot text here at every wake
DOUT and the 5V and GND pads beside it stay empty
of the hall switch are soldered
to these two pads of the reader.
Only with the AH3661UA hall switch
at the controller: its output only pulls low
at the switch, across its supply legs
Only if card detection has to wake the ball
D2, D3: BAT43 or 1N5817, in place of the plain wire to A1
1. Every ground symbol is one net. Each ground wire ends at OUT− of the charger, the star point.
Nothing but the cell is connected to B+ and B−.
2. Tags of one name, VBAT or +5V, are one net. +5V is live only while the controller holds En high.
3. R4 and R5 keep the 5 V rail and the amplifier switched off whenever the controller does not drive them:
at reset, while it is flashed, and asleep. Both boards carry a pull-up to the battery, so the two
resistors have to be this small.
4. R3 keeps the reader in power-down while the controller sleeps.
5. C2 is soldered at the Vin pad of the boost converter, C3 at the servo, R1, R2 and C1 at pad D1.
one of the nine small pads (1.27 mm) on the underside of the XIAO
wires that are joined; wires that only cross have no dot
